args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback: service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 was promoted. Follow-up needed: find the root cause in v2.3.1 and review why an unhealthy RC was promoted.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** I moved checkout-api from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. I skipped v2.3.1-rc because it only ran in staging and was unhealthy there too.
- **Result:** After the rollback, the service passes its health checks and the error rate is down from about 18% to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery.

The incident also flags two follow-ups: finding what broke in v2.3.1, and asking why it went to production even though its release candidate was already unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
